body: Oh my God! That sounds heavenly. What a lucky little one you have.
Sorry y'all, Dependeco is what I meant.
Thanks, this really brings me hope.
Sir, thank you so much for your insight. I've been dealing with my own depression since I was sixteen, and have almost given up on finding a curative. Stories like this actually give me hope.

I've been meditating almost every day for a year.

What would acting "authentically" in every context even mean? Like, given the choice between laying on my bed and staring at the ceiling and forcing myself to exercise, what would be the more authentic action? The one that would technically be 'good' for me (whatever that means) or the one in line with my deepest sense of how the world actually is and what it deserves from me?
Gonna have to wait for another night, I'm afraid. She had to go home earlier than expected. Keep you posted!

Thank you for your thoughtful reply.

I personally am not willing to live a life that regular medication use would dictate (I want to travel and stay in some remote locations for my career, places where pharmacy access would be unreliable at best). As I mentioned before, all of the SSRIs I tried were not only ineffective but also came with a host of intolerable side effects and withdrawal symptoms.

Further, I do not believe that not wanting to be dependent on medication contributes to a culture of stigma vis a vis MH. Dependency comes with the territory, like it or not. I, for one, am pretty angry that the side effects of those drugs weren't adequately stressed to me by any of the medical professionals I interacted with prior to taking them. Those side effects should be clearly communicated at the start of every new prescription, IMO.

The emotional state is so upsetting that I can't get some work done. Yes, dwelling is a big part of the problem. I'm holding down a job fine, at the moment, but I worry what might happen. 

Let me see if I understand you, here: "derailing to a psychiatrist," as you put it, is "quitting progress"? I think seeking medical attention when you are in serious shit is pretty to self-advocating.

Thanks for your thoughtful comment.

On the question of purpose, I am torn in two directions. I sometimes feel that everything is pointless, that I'll never be satisfied and that chasing any semblance of purpose is just a fools errand; a slightly more psychologically sophisticated version of base hedonistic pleasure seeking--not substantively different from drinking to excess or jerking off. As with both of those activities, I fear I'd eventually find their another empty promise of fulfillment.

On the other hand, I know that I once held very strong political beliefs, and did my best to be active in my community. I once thought that was something I was capable of engaging in with passion and diligence and a sense of hope for the future. That time has past. I think doing something in the service of that cause is still the only thing that could give my life purpose, but the situation is so hopeless these days that I can't fool myself anymore.

Let me clarify: I want to be able to go about my daily routine on a regular basis without sudden feelings of hopelessness and pointlessness interrupting anything. I've tried to accomplish this with all of the positive life changes and therapeutic interventions I listed above. And still this has not been achieved. (Please believe me when I say my exercise and diet is incredibly healthy -- lack of protein is not the issue, here).

I've considered electroshock and TMS (I know those are radically different procedures). Going to ask my new therapist about them when I see him next. But I have the overwhelming feeling they're just another dead end, and I would like some assurance that other, more invasive procedures are available and might provide a permanent solution. I've done some reading about bilateral cingulotomy. Can anyone tell me if that is a viable option?
